messages:
maria_support: Customer (acct acme-001) opened a billing dispute: invoice INV-20260077 shows 120 reserved GPU hours on eu-west-1-dedicated-3 for 2026-03-14, but their dashboard shows ~24h and token usage is tiny. Can someone triage?

sanjay_billing: Ack, tagging finance. Do we have pool-level metering raw rows? Also which timezone/billing window did they quote?

maria_support: They supplied dashboard screenshots and a CSV. They say the dashboard window is '2026-03-14 00:00 - 2026-03-14 23:59 UTC'. Invoice seems to have captured 2026-03-14 22:00 -> 2026-03-15 02:00 extra burn.

eli_infra: Quick check - I'll grep autoscaler and warmup logs for that pool and window. Suspect warmup/warm VM lifecycle counted against reserved hours due to a rounding bug in hourly aggregation.

metering-bot: Metering snapshot for acme-001 / eu-west-1-dedicated-3 (2026-03-14 00:00 -> 2026-03-15 03:00 UTC): reserved_hours_reported=120, gpu_minutes_aggregated=7200, token_count=10124, burst_fallback_used=0, warmup_instance_minutes=360. Note: aggregation granularity=1h, rounding_mode=ceil.

eli_infra: Repro query I ran against meter-db: 
```
SELECT sum(ceil(active_minutes/60.0)) as billed_hours
FROM reserved_instance_activity
WHERE pool='eu-west-1-dedicated-3' AND account_id='acme-001'
AND ts >= '2026-03-14' AND ts < '2026-03-15';
```
Result: billed_hours = 120. Raw active_minutes sum = 5440 (== 90.666.. hours). Rounding to hour ceiling per-instance per-hour bucket explains the overshoot but not all of it.

maria_support: So warmup_instance_minutes=360 (6h) explains part; but customer still sees 24h on app dashboard. Is dashboard using continuous sampling and not per-instance ceil?

eli_infra: Correct, dashboard uses per-pool continuous metric (total_active_minutes/60) without per-instance ceil. Metering pipeline currently does per-instance ceil before summing to enforce minimum billable hour per instance-hour, but there's a bug where health-check instances (type=warmup) were not excluded from ceil.

finance_escalation: Thanks — can we calculate a proposed credit? If billed 120h but continuous would be 90.67h, propose credit = (120 - 90.67) * unit_price. Also should exclude warmup 6h from ceil: adjusted_billed = 120 - (ceil(360/60) - (360/60)). That's ~120 - (6 - 6) -> no change in that naive math; but we should instead ensure warmup minutes counted as fractional.

eli_infra: Plan: patch aggregator to exempt instances with label 'warmup' from per-instance ceiling and re-run invoice rollup for acme-001; write a temporary rollback script to recompute billable_hours = floor(total_active_minutes/60 * 100)/100 to avoid double rounding. I'll create PR and run test on staging.

maria_support: Customer asked for ETA on credit — can we give provisional timeline?

finance_escalation: If patch + re-roll goes smoothly we'll have corrected hours and a draft credit note by EOD UTC today (2026-03-15). If re-roll touches the invoice system it may require manual approval. I'll queue a priority review.

eli_infra: Added short repro for QA: spin a dedicated pool with one warmup instance for 6 minutes, one normal instance for 54 minutes in same hour, and ensure the meter pipeline aggregates. Expect billed_hours (current buggy) = 2; expected corrected billed_hours = 1.

maria_support: Copying customer-facing note to send after finance confirms: "We're investigating a metering aggregation issue that caused per-instance hourly-ceil to count warmup/health-check instances. We're reprocessing your hour totals and will issue a credit if we confirm overbilling. ETA: EOD UTC." :thumbsup:

finance_escalation: Created ticket FIN-2026-342 with priority P1 and linked invoice. Will update once re-roll complete.

eli_infra: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1287. Running integration job now.

maria_support: Thanks all. I'll keep customer updated and attach FIN-2026-342.

sanjay_billing: One more ask — add the raw meter export CSV to ticket and include a column 'instance_label' so we can forensics later.

maria_support: Added CSV to FIN-2026-342 and pinged customer that we're working on it.
